renunciation

/rih-nun-see-AY-shun/ · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Renunciation means the formal, deliberate giving up of a right, claim, title, or belief.

Signing the oath at the consulate, Priya completed her renunciation of her old citizenship, knowing the decision was permanent.

Example

When Marcus left the firm he had co-founded, his renunciation of any future claim to its profits was spelled out in a signed agreement.

Renunciation fits because Marcus is formally and deliberately giving up a legal claim — a share of future profits — and the act is made official in a signed document, not just a casual decision to walk away.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

disavowal: A disavowal formally denies any connection to or responsibility for something — a campaign disavows a supporter's remarks: 'that is not ours.' Renunciation gives up something that genuinely is yours — a right, title, or belief you admit you hold and now formally release. Disavowal says it was never mine; renunciation says it is mine no longer.

surrender: Surrender is the act of handing over or giving up something you held, often because pressure or defeat leaves little choice. Renunciation is deliberate and declared: a formal, often written act of giving up a right, claim, or belief of your own free will. Armies surrender; monks and ex-monarchs make renunciations.

abandonment: Abandonment is giving something up completely and leaving it behind — walking away from a car, a plan, a post — with no ceremony and no formal declaration. Renunciation is the opposite in style: a solemn, declared, often signed act of giving up a right, claim, or belief.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

retention: keeping possession of something

assertion: actively claiming or insisting on a right

Where it sits · how much is being surrendered — waiver → renunciation → abdication

waiver vs. renunciation: A waiver is weaker — it gives up one specific right, often as routine paperwork, without renunciation's sense of a solemn, life-changing break.

abdication vs. renunciation: Abdication is stronger — it is the renunciation of the highest office itself, surrendering not just a single claim but supreme power.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — re-

Prefix — re-: back, away (Latin)

Root — nunci

Root — nunci: to announce, to report (Latin nuntiare, from nuntius, 'messenger')

Suffix — -ation

Suffix — -ation: the act or process of (noun-forming)

Put it together

Put it together: Renunciation is literally 'the act of announcing back/away' — you officially announce that you are sending a right, claim, or belief away from yourself, which is why the word implies a formal declaration rather than quietly quitting.

Use the root in a new word: enunciate

Use the root in a new word: enunciate: The debate coach reminded Amara to enunciate whenever nerves made her rush.

Word Choice

Formal / legal & religious

Renunciation is a formal, official word — it appears in citizenship law, legal filings, and religious life, and it implies a deliberate, declared act. You make a renunciation of a claim, title, belief, or allegiance; giving up snacks for a week is just quitting, not a renunciation.
